domain.quantified: Every non-proxied plain-value input satisfying the published TypeScript shapes and every guard in the complete normalized equations; no fixture or finite-sample restriction.
domain.exactness: Quantities, units, revision ids, active pointers, graph membership, root/revision digests, and SHA-256 words use the exact equations and rejection branches; there is no epsilon arithmetic.
domain.storage: Only fresh local arrays, maps, sets, typed arrays, records, or a newly allocated InventoryCatalog instance are mutated; caller-owned inputs and retained catalog state remain read-only.
domain.builtins: Array, Map, Set, Object, Number, Math, String, TextEncoder, Uint8Array, Uint32Array, BigInt, and Error operations resolve to real installed TypeScript standard-library declarations and use ordinary unmodified runtime semantics.
domain.callbacks: The private revision-family merge invokes only its two named parameters; the public extension equation binds every call to an inline revision-id projection and one exact independently checked revision-digest equation.

excluded: Proxies, accessors, subclasses, monkey-patched built-ins, custom collection/string/typed-array lookalikes, and own-property method shadowing.
Concurrent mutation of inputs, catalog values, prototypes, or the source compiler snapshot during a call.
Calling the private generic merge helper outside the exact bindings present in extendInventoryCatalog.

laws.equation: Definitions validate exact identities, measurement axes and units, tracking, positive quantities, duplicate ids, graph membership and cycles before recursively cloning and freezing every retained value.

Complete catalog construction normalizes every revision family, rejects missing or mismatched active revisions, builds exact lookup maps, sorts all retained families, validates package/composition/collection graphs, and fingerprints the resulting immutable catalog.

Snapshot loading recomputes and checks the exact root digest; retention compares every retained revision digest; extension merges identical revisions, rejects changed identities, moves only supplied active pointers, and preserves object identity for an unchanged digest.

Revision and root digests include every meaning-bearing field in fixed order, sort unordered records and revision families, preserve the legacy empty-transformation root shape, and use the complete built-in-free SHA-256 equation.

Position validation enforces required and forbidden lot/serial identities and rejects undeclared qualified dimensions; fungibility lookups return exactly one retained revision or throw their exact unknown-identity error.
